newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Higher on firmer swaps and crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Higher on firmer swaps and crude.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market firmed on the back of swaps and crude gains despite the continued absence of Chinese buyers, traders said on Wednesday.
One trader said Kuwait Petroleum Corp was likely to offer additional spot cargoes to Singapore in April.
"Supplies are still fairly sufficient and I think we will be pretty okay until April," the trader said.
But expectations for fresh demand pushed prices higher, the trader said.

"The market will depend largely on China, which is still staying on the sidelines," another trader said, adding that China had covered the first half of March and might remain inactive until early next month.
"For Asia, there has been no fundamental changes and sentiment is still quite bearish," the trader added.
Fuel oil swaps were higher with March quoted at $100.50/$101.50, up from Tuesday's $98.50/$99.5. March traded earlier in the day at $100.50 per tonne.
April swaps also firmed to $99.50/$100.50 per tonne from Tuesday's $97/$98.
Firm fuel oil swaps and crude gains also triggered active trading interest in the bunker market, pushing prices for 380-cst $3 higher per tonne, traders said.
"Demand is coming back to the market slowly though China is still inactive," said one major.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
